solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Robust force from Spanish and Babylonian cities

parts.note: Vigo is a port city in Galicia, Spain
Ur was an ancient city of Sumer and Babylonia, the 'cities' plural covering both pieces

explanation.surface: A historian describes the sheer might drawn from ancient and Spanish cities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spanish and Babylonian cities' gives two cities, one from each place: Vigo in Spain and Ur in ancient Mesopotamia.
explanation.definitionFit: Vigour is energetic strength, a robust force of body or mind.

clue.text: You could say we admitted to sick satire

indicators.note: admitted to means let inside, so one piece goes within the other
sick suggests something unwell or twisted, so the letters of satire are reworked

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
taken as written

explanation.surface: A comedian concedes, in a manner of speaking, that their satire was sick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You could say' looks like a link phrase introducing the wordplay, but it is the definition: the answer is a hedging expression.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a verbal hedge meaning 'so to speak', which is what 'you could say' expresses.

clue.text: Group cutting worst records ruined me

indicators.note: cutting means slicing into, so the group goes inside the rearranged letters
ruined says the letters of worst records are wrecked and rebuilt in another order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
a set is a group of things

explanation.surface: Someone laments that a band breaking into the charts with dreadful records has ruined them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' turns WORST RECORDS into CROSSWORDTER, and 'cutting' drops SET into it. 'me' is the setter speaking of themselves, a common crossword self-reference.
explanation.definitionFit: The puzzle's author refers to themself as 'me', and that author is the compiler of the clues.

clue.text: Hunter in exploit over enormously long period

indicators.note: in a down answer, over places the first piece above the second

parts.note: an exploit is a deed or act
an aeon is an immensely long span of time

explanation.surface: A hunter is engaged in some exploit lasting an age.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Actaeon was a hunter who saw Artemis bathing and was turned into a stag.
explanation.definitionFit: Actaeon is the huntsman of Greek legend, torn apart by his own hounds.

clue.text: Plato with commission to destabilise global view

indicators.note: destabilising something knocks it out of order, so these letters are thrown into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A philosopher is commissioned to unsettle an outlook on the world.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosmopolitanism is the outlook of a citizen of the world, a worldwide rather than local perspective.

clue.text: Incredibly small alpha male in charge

parts.note: A is the letter alpha in the phonetic alphabet
a tom is a male animal, especially a cat

explanation.surface: A tiny dominant male animal is running the show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alpha male' looks like one phrase, but alpha gives A and male gives TOM separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Atomic, in informal use, means minute, as tiny as an atom.

clue.text: Depressed daughter to have drink at speed

definitions.meaning: to gulp a drink in one go

parts.note: to own something is to have it

explanation.surface: A gloomy girl takes to knocking back her drinks quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: Two definitions sit either side of the wordplay: 'Depressed' at the start and 'drink at speed' at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling low is being blue, and to gulp a pint quickly is to sink it in one.

clue.text: Good results with point to secure at home

indicators.note: securing something means holding it fast, so the first pieces wrap round the second

parts.note: S is a compass point, south
in means at home, as in staying in

explanation.surface: A team secures good results with a point at its home ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Victories are the good results a team hopes for.

clue.text: Men returning caught enormous bird

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word for men is read backwards

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Soldiers coming back have captured a huge bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The roc is the giant mythical bird of the Arabian Nights, able to carry off elephants.

clue.text: Choice to turn it on after surgery

indicators.note: after puts the rearranged letters behind the surgery piece

parts.note: OP is short for operation, a piece of surgery

indicators.note: turn signals the letters being turned about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: After an operation a patient may choose to switch a device back on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' is the anagram signal, not a switch being turned; 'to' simply links definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An option is something one may select, a choice.

clue.text: Old Spaniard in firm runs trial that's incomplete

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: incomplete means lacking its end, so the last letter of the word for trial is dropped

parts.note: a test is a trial

explanation.surface: An old Spaniard works in a firm running a trial that never finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: Hernán Cortés was the 16th-century conquistador who overthrew the Aztec empire.
explanation.definitionFit: Cortés is the conquistador who conquered Mexico, a Spaniard of history.

clue.text: Military force works to contain Frenchman having last word

indicators.note: containing means holding within, so the other pieces go inside the word for works

parts.note: art is creative work, works of art
M is short for Monsieur, a Frenchman
amen is the word that ends a prayer

explanation.surface: An army's artworks include a Frenchman who always insists on the final say.
explanation.definitionFit: Armament means the weapons and forces a nation holds for war.

clue.text: One knocking forest spirits?

parts.note: greenwood is a forest in leaf, as in Robin Hood's haunt
pecker means courage or spirits, as in 'keep your pecker up', a British idiom

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a knocking sound in the woods comes from ghosts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keep your pecker up' is British slang for 'stay cheerful'. 'spirits' suggests ghosts in a forest, but it means morale.
explanation.definitionFit: This bird drums its beak against tree trunks, so it is something that knocks.

clue.text: Beast taking zig-zag course?

parts.note: the strokes of the three capital letters, written out, trace a zig-zag line, so the animal's name follows such a course

explanation.surface: An animal weaves a wavering path across a field.
explanation.walkthrough: Drawn as capitals, the letters of this short animal name make a zig-zag shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A female sheep is a farm beast, and its name in capitals zig-zags on the page.

clue.text: Wine produced by Middle Eastern country endlessly

parts.note: made means produced

indicators.note: endlessly means without its end, so the final letter of the country is lost

parts.note: Iran is a country in the Middle East

explanation.surface: A wine produced in a Middle Eastern country.
explanation.definitionFit: Madeira is a fortified wine from the Portuguese island of that name.

clue.text: Turkish commander edges away from infidel

indicators.note: taking the edges away means removing the first and last letters of the word for infidel

parts.note: a pagan is an unbeliever, an infidel

explanation.surface: A Turkish commander backs away from an unbeliever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'edges away' looks like a cautious retreat but it strips the outer letters from PAGAN.
explanation.definitionFit: An aga was an Ottoman title for a military officer or chief.

clue.text: Staines Massif character Scots hooligan put straight

parts.note: Ali G is Sacha Baron Cohen's comic character, leader of the Staines Massif gang in a town west of London
ned is Scottish slang for a young hooligan

explanation.surface: A comedy character and a Scottish thug have been put straight.
explanation.walkthrough: Ali G, a would-be gangster from Staines, Surrey, was the TV creation of Sacha Baron Cohen.
explanation.definitionFit: Aligned means brought into line, set straight.

clue.text: Big Chief Iron Cuckoo enters stone circle

indicators.note: enters means goes inside, so the jumbled letters sit within stone and circle

parts.note: a gem is a precious stone
O is shaped like a circle

indicators.note: cuckoo means crazy, so the letters of iron are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A tribal leader with a crazy iron bird walks into a stone circle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cuckoo' looks like a bird beside 'Big Chief', but it is the anagram signal; the shuffled letters split GEM from O.
explanation.definitionFit: Geronimo was a renowned Apache leader, a great chief of his people.

clue.text: Waller took top tip from Roach — piano's inside

parts.note: had means took, as in had lunch

indicators.note: the top tip in a down answer is the first letter of the word roach
inside means the inner letters, without the outer ones, of the word piano

parts.note: read as piano is, the word piano itself

explanation.surface: Fats Waller, the jazz pianist, took a tip from a fish, with piano in the background.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waller' suggests Fats Waller the jazz pianist, which 'piano' reinforces; it means a builder of a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman emperor ordered the great wall across northern Britain, so he is a builder of walls.

clue.text: What might give heart a big shock?

definitions.text: What might give heart a big shock?

parts.words: What might give heart a big shock?
parts.note: rearranging the letters of heart produces the planet's name, so heart has had a shattering jolt

explanation.surface: Something that might give a person's heart a terrible fright.
explanation.walkthrough: Read cryptically, shattering the word 'heart' gives the planet's name; the whole is an adjective for something momentous.
explanation.definitionFit: Something huge enough to shake the world gives anyone a big shock.

clue.text: Mike cuts Roman flower in wood

indicators.note: cuts means slices into, so the letter goes inside the river

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river: the Tiber runs through Rome
Mike is M in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Mike cuts a Roman flower growing in the woods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is read as 'one that flows', a river, not a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Timber is wood cut for building.

clue.text: Sewer, lake and river up in north-east

indicators.note: in places the reversed letters inside the compass point
in a down answer, up means read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland

explanation.surface: A drain, a lake and a river are surveyed in the north-east of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sewer' reads as a drain, but it means one who sews. 'up' reverses L and DEE to EEDL.
explanation.definitionFit: A tool used for sewing is a sewer in the sense of something that sews.

clue.text: Membrane found defective in a primate

indicators.note: defective means faulty, so the letters of a primate are broken and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A faulty membrane is discovered in an ape.
explanation.definitionFit: The pia mater is the delicate innermost membrane covering the brain and spinal cord.

clue.text: Small measure taken to rein in a cleric

indicators.note: reining in means holding back within limits, so the a goes inside the measure

parts.note: 1 mm, one millimetre, written as I then MM

explanation.surface: A small measure is taken to keep a religious leader in check.
explanation.walkthrough: The small measure is '1 mm', with the digit 1 read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: An imam leads prayers in a mosque, a Muslim cleric.

clue.text: Bum around new French location

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the word for bum goes round the letter

parts.note: nates is the anatomical word for the buttocks

explanation.surface: A layabout loafs around a new place in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bum' suggests a loafer but means the buttocks, NATES.
explanation.definitionFit: Nantes is a city in western France on the Loire.

clue.text: Composer changes not one note, ultimately

indicators.note: not says the word for one is left out of the word for changes

parts.note: varies means changes
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: ultimately means at the very end, so the last letter of note is taken

explanation.surface: A composer revises his score, removing a single note at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: Edgard Varèse was a French-born modernist composer who worked in America.
explanation.definitionFit: Varèse wrote experimental orchestral works such as Ionisation, so he is a composer.

clue.text: Blockhead in Obama's shoes

indicators.note: in shows the letters lie within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone says only a fool would want to step into the President's shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: A fool or dimwit is called a donkey in insult.

clue.text: Secret agent necessarily underground?

definitions.meaning: a spy planted inside an organisation
a burrowing mammal must live below the surface, as a spy must stay hidden

explanation.surface: A spy has to work out of sight, underground.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is a playful one: the animal lives underground by nature, while the spy works 'underground' figuratively.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep-cover spy and a burrowing animal share one name.
